I am an old woman here in Pemba, and I have grown rice on this small piece for many years. I do not have money for the fertilizer in the bag — those things are for people with cash, and the shop is far. I will plant the seed I kept from last harvest like my mother taught me, and I will use the cow manure my neighbor gives me when his animals come near. My daughter and grandchildren help me in the field, and at transplanting time I call two women from the village to help me finish before the rain stops.
